item.title: Nonzero solutions for Dirichlet problems with the competing (p,q)-Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2611.08624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The following equation is considered: $$-\Delta_p u(\boldsymbol{x}) + \Delta_q u(\boldsymbol{x}) = f\big(\boldsymbol{x}, u(\boldsymbol{x})\big)\text{ for } \boldsymbol{x} \in \Omega, \qquad u(\boldsymbol{x}) = 0 \text{ for } \boldsymbol{x}\in \partial \Omega.$$ We start by showing that the energy functional associated with the considered problem no longer has the properties typical of its non-competing counterpart, which prevents a direct application of standard variational and monotonicity methods. Using Ekeland's variational principle combined with properties imposed on the nonlinear term~$f$, we prove the existence of a nonzero generalized solution to the problem. It is also shown that in the one-dimensional case $\Omega = (-1,1)$, assuming that $f$ satisfies the symmetry conditions $$f(x,u) = f(-x,u) = -f(x,-u),$$ together with the sign condition $f(x,u) \geq 0$ for $u \geq 0$ and an appropriate growth bound on $f$, a convex relaxation of the action functional yields the existence of a positive weak solution. Furthermore, we prove that in this setting, and under a slightly stronger sign condition $$f(x,u) > 0\text{ for }u > 0,$$ all global minimizers of the action functional do not vanish in $(-1,1)$ but fail to be of class $C^1$.
item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Be{\l}dzi\'nski

item.title: Regularity of elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.08635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study autonomous elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure of the form \[ -\operatorname{div}\big(\mathfrak a(|Du|)Du\big)=0 \quad \text{in }\ \Omega\subset \mathbb R^n \] Under two-sided quantitative $(p,q)$-growth conditions on $\mathfrak a$, we prove gradient H\"older continuity with constants and exponent depending only on the dimensions, $p$ and $q$. This improves the classical theory initiated by Uhlenbeck by removing the continuity requirement on $\mathfrak a'$. The proof uses nonlinear comparison systems whose regularity follows from a scalar uniformly elliptic equation. Under weaker $(p,q)$-growth conditions on the convex function $\varphi(t):=\int_0^t s\mathfrak a(s)\,ds$, we obtain local $W^{1,s}$-regularity for every $s>1$, and hence H\"older continuity of solutions with every exponent less than one. An additional lower growth condition on $\mathfrak a$ yields local Lipschitz continuity, even when $\mathfrak a$ is discontinuous.
item.dc:creator: Jihoon Ok

item.title: Blow-Up and Life-Span for Nonlinear Hardy-H\'enon Parabolic Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the nonlinear Hardy-H\'enon parabolic equation $ u_t=\Delta u+|x|^l|u|^\alpha u,$ $t>0,$ $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$ or $x\in\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}$, with $N\ge1$, $l>-\min\{2,N\}$, $\alpha>0$, with nonnegative initial datum $u_0$. We first establish new criteria for finite-time blow-up. We then derive optimal upper bounds for the life-span $T_{\max}(\lambda\varphi)$ of solutions arising from the initial datum $u_0=\lambda\varphi$. These estimates establish a precise dependence of $T_{\max}(\lambda\varphi)$ on both the initial profile $\varphi$ and the parameter $\lambda$ in the small and large-amplitude regimes.
item.dc:creator: Byrame Ben Slimene, Slim Tayachi

item.title: Non-conical classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated singularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.08670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several examples of one-homogeneous classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated free boundary singularity are known. Adapting the approach of Caffarelli, Hardt, and Simon for minimal surfaces, we construct non-conical classical solutions with an isolated free boundary singularity by perturbing a one-homogeneous solution $U$. Moreover, if $U$ is strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate), then any solution sufficiently close to $U$ is also strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate).
item.dc:creator: Minyoung Jeong

item.title: Regularity of Weak Solutions near Singular Minimizing Cones for the One-Phase Free Boundary Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.08688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alt and Caffarelli proved an Allard-type $\epsilon$-regularity theorem near the flat one-homogeneous minimizer of the one-phase free boundary problem. A natural follow-up question is whether an analogous regularity result holds near singular minimizing cones. In this paper, we prove such an $\epsilon$-regularity theorem near a strongly integrable one-phase minimizing cone with an isolated singularity. More precisely, we show that, after a suitable translation and rotation, the free boundary of any non-degenerate weak solution sufficiently close to the cone is graphical over the free boundary of a leaf of the De Silva--Jerison--Shahgholian foliation. This result is analogous to recent $\epsilon$-regularity theorems in minimal surface theory by Edelen and by Edelen--Spolaor; our proof adapts the strategy of Edelen to the one-phase setting.
item.dc:creator: Minyoung Jeong

item.title: Global regularity of the two-dimensional fractional Boussinesq equations with critical dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the present paper, our primary focus is on the Boussinesq equations with fractional velocity dissipation $\Lambda^\alpha u$ and temperature diffusion $\Lambda^\beta\theta$. On the critical balance line $\alpha+\beta=1$, establishing global regularity for weak velocity dissipation has been obstructed by the quadratic convective-buoyancy feedback, and all available results below $\alpha=\frac{10}{13}$ require a smallness assumption on the initial temperature. In this paper, we prove large-data global regularity across the extended regime $\alpha>\frac{\sqrt{57}-5}{4} \approx 0.637$. This provides a step beyond the previous barrier $\alpha=\frac{10}{13}$, unconditionally dismantling the temperature smallness assumption that has persisted in the literature for over a decade. The mathematical mechanism relies on a high-order Quadratic Normal Form transformation $H=\omega-R_{\alpha}\theta-\Bop(\theta,\theta)$ tailored to eliminate non-resonant quadratic vorticity-temperature interactions. Crucially, by uncovering the exact physical scalings of the underlying multilinear commutators and maintaining sharp fractional conjugates in the $L^m$-energy framework, we ensure that the global energy closure is governed entirely by the quadratic thermal dissipation. Once an integrability threshold $m>\frac{2}{\alpha}$ is attained, a fine Littlewood-Paley transport estimate drives a fractional regularity gain $H \in B_{r,\infty}^{3\alpha-2}$, ensuring the velocity field achieves critical drift regularity $C^{\alpha}$. By Silvestre-type drift regularization, this spontaneously generates positive H\"older continuity for the temperature, which in turn elevates the drift regularity strictly beyond the critical threshold, unlocking non-local Schauder estimates to prevent finite-time singularity formation.
item.dc:creator: Qian Li, Jiahong Wu, Xiaojing Xu, Zhuan Ye

item.title: On nonlocal geometric rigidity estimates in bounded uniform domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.08888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove fractional geometric rigidity estimates and fractional Korn's first inequalities with general singular weights in bounded uniform domains in $\mathbb R^n.$ The classical choice of the energy well $SO(n)$ for the geometric rigidity estimate fails due to the lack of a notion of orientation for Lebesgue fields. The remedy is to choose $O(n)$ as the energy well. Due to the recently developed theory of local-to-nonlocal passage of rigidity estimates developed by the first author, both estimates reduce to the analogous local estimates on the cube, which we prove in several steps by compactness and linearization arguments.
item.dc:creator: Davit Harutyunyan, Hayk Mikayelyan

item.title: Sharp condition for Superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the sharp condition for local superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation $(-\Delta)^m u=u^{(n+2m)/(n-2m)}$, where $m\geq2$ is an integer and $n>2m$. For a solution in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at zero, local superharmonicity holds if and only if $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)>0$. The threshold is sharp. In the biharmonic case $m=2$, for every $n\geq5$, we construct smooth positive solutions of $\Delta^2u=u^{(n+4)/(n-4)}$ in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at $0$, satisfying $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)=0$ and $\limsup_{x\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, while $-\Delta u$ converges to a finite negative limit along a fixed ray. The construction relies on an infinite array of concentrating bubbles arranged on concentric polygons, with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction controlling their interactions against a vanishing background.
item.dc:creator: Xia Huang, Yuan Li, Yixing Pu

item.title: Critical Resonance and the Radial Branch in Maz'ya's Weighted Hessian--Gradient Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.09009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the sharp constant $C(p,\gamma)$ in Maz'ya's planar weighted inequality \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|\nabla\psi|^p|x|^{p(\gamma-1)}\, \mathrm{d} x \le C(p,\gamma)\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|D^2\psi|_{\mathrm{F}}^p|x|^{p\gamma}\, \mathrm{d} x, \] where $|\cdot|_{\mathrm{F}}$ denotes the Frobenius norm. For every fixed $1\le p<\infty$, with $a=\gamma-1+2/p$, we prove \[ C(p,\gamma)^{-1}=2^{p/2}|a|^p+O_p(|a|^{p+1})\qquad(a\to0). \] The leading term comes from the first angular harmonics after the Emden--Fowler transform. We also determine explicit exterior parameter rays on which the unrestricted constant equals the radial value $(1+a^2)^{-p/2}$. The proof uses an entropy identity and a homogeneous calibration. In the remaining transition region, we obtain symmetry-breaking intervals and a necessary and sufficient condition for nonnegativity of the periodic second variation at the radial state. An explicit example shows that global symmetry breaking can occur even when this second variation is nonnegative.
item.dc:creator: Suman Das

item.title: Delaunay classification of positive singular solutions to the critical Lane--Emden system
item.description: arXiv:2611.09029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify positive classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system \begin{align*} \begin{cases} -\Delta u=v^p & ~~\text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\},\\ -\Delta v=u^q &~~ \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}, \end{cases} \end{align*} with a nonremovable singularity at $0$ (i.e., $\lim_{x\to0}u(x)=\lim_{x\to0}v(x)=+\infty$), where $n\ge3$ and $p,q>0$ satisfy \[ \frac1{p+1}+\frac1{q+1}=\frac{n-2}{n}. \] Without additional growth or integrability assumptions, we establish radial symmetry about the origin, strict radial decrease, and global two-sided power bounds for both components. Furthermore, every such solution can be written as \[ u(x)=|x|^{-\alpha}U(\log|x|),\qquad v(x)=|x|^{-\beta}V(\log|x|), \] where $\alpha=\frac{n}{q+1}$, $\beta=\frac{n}{p+1}$, and $(U,V)$ is either the positive equilibrium $(A,B)=((\frac{\alpha}{\beta})^{\frac{\alpha}{2}}, (\frac{\alpha}{\beta})^{\frac{\beta}{2}})$ or a positive nonconstant periodic solution of the associated Emden--Fowler system. These periodic solutions form a Delaunay family: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,A)$, there is a unique profile pair, up to translation in $t=\log|x|$, with $\min_{\mathbb{R}}U=\varepsilon$. The Hamiltonian energy provides an alternative parameter, decreasing continuously and strictly from zero to the equilibrium energy as $\varepsilon$ increases from $0$ to $A$. The common least period of the two components tends to infinity as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and to the period of the linearized oscillation at $(A,B)$ as $\varepsilon\uparrow A$. The classification includes the case of a sublinear exponent.
item.dc:creator: Xia Huang, Yahui Jiang, Feng Zhou, Xianmei Zhou

item.title: Complete uniqueness for two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.09070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alt, Caffarelli and Friedman established the existence of two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows in [Asymmetric jet flows. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 35, 29--68, 1982]. In their formulation, the constant fluid speed $\lambda$ on the free boundaries and the downstream asymptotic angle $\theta$ are selected as part of the solution. In this paper, we prove that the asymmetric jet is unique for a prescribed nozzle and mass flux. We first establish the strict vertical monotonicity of the stream function $u$ and introduce the partial hodograph coordinates $\xi=x$ and $\eta=u(x,y)$, which map every fluid domain onto the same fixed strip. Under this framework, each jet is characterized by a height function $y=h(\xi,\eta)$, which determines the vertical position along the streamline $u=\eta$ at horizontal coordinate $\xi$. By analyzing the difference between the height functions of two candidate jets on this strip, we derive an elliptic equation with Dirichlet conditions on the fixed walls and conormal conditions on the free boundaries. Combining these mixed boundary conditions with the asymptotic behaviors, we first establish the uniqueness of the free-boundary fluid speed $\lambda$. For the resulting common speed, a local perturbation of the height function near a nozzle endpoint, together with the maximum principle, proves that the two height functions must coincide. Inverting the partial hodograph transformation then establishes the uniqueness of the physical jet.
item.dc:creator: Jianfeng Cheng, Zikang Gu

item.title: Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: The Reaction-Flux Landscape and Maximizing Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2611.09127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue our study of a PDE-constrained variational model for maximizing the total reaction flux by optimizing the spatial distribution of catalytic materials, such as enzymes. The total amount of enzyme is fixed, and the substrate concentration is governed by a reaction-diffusion equation with prescribed boundary values. We consider both linear and nonlinear Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics. In previous work, we constructed a maximizing sequence, computed the first and second variations of the reaction functional, and established the nonexistence of local maximizers. Here, we conduct a more comprehensive analysis. We prove that the functional is strictly concave for linear kinetics but need not be concave or convex for nonlinear kinetics. We also show that no critical points exist. We then characterize maximizing sequences and identify all their possible limiting measures. Our analysis reveals the mechanism of reaction maximization through spatial localization: maximizing sequences concentrate enzymes near the portion of the boundary where the substrate concentration is largest. Moreover, the landscape of the functional defining the total reaction differs between the linear and nonlinear cases, a point less emphasized in applications. Consistent with existing biophysical studies, these findings motivate the development and analysis of regularized models.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Yasir Feroz Khan, Bo Li

item.title: On the optimal mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled to the Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.09160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In the absence of fluid interaction, the classical Keller-Segel system admits a well-known $4\pi$-critical-mass dichotomy: for every suitably regular initial datum of total mass \(m<4\pi\), the associated no-flux initial-boundary value problem admits a global bounded classical solution, whereas for \(m>4\pi\), there exist smooth initial configurations of mass $m$ such that the associated solution blows up in finite or infinite time. For the fluid-coupled system, Winkler first established global generalized solvability under the condition \(m<2\pi\) and proposed an open question whether the fluid action may lower the critical blow-up mass to some value lying between $2\pi$ and $4\pi$. In the present work, we resolve this open problem and show that the presence of the fluid does not alter the critical mass threshold, and the entire classical subcritical regime remains intact: every admissible initial datum with total mass \(m<4\pi\) generates a unique global classical solution that is uniformly bounded with respect to time. Our proof relies on the construction of a new quasi-energy inequality. The key underlying observation is that combining relative isoperimetric estimates with rearrangement techniques yields a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality on bounded planar domains with an explicit leading constant.
item.dc:creator: Lili Du, Yulan Wang, Yichen Zhang

item.title: Positive self-similar solutions of a parabolic equation with spatially weighted absorption in a half-space
item.description: arXiv:2611.09179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study positive solutions of $u_t-\Delta u+x_1^{2\alpha}|u|^{q-1}u=0$ in the half-space $\{x_1>0\}$, with $\alpha>-1$ and $q>1$, vanishing on $\{x_1=0\}$ and at $t=0$ away from the origin. Let $q_c=(N+3+2\alpha)/(N+1)$. For $1<q<q_c$ we prove that there is exactly one positive self-similar solution continuous away from the origin, and that its profile satisfies Gaussian bounds that are sharp up to multiplicative constants. For $q\ge q_c$ there is none. We also show that, after removing the Gaussian factor, the profile has an angular limit shape $\Phi$ in every mode, give an integral formula for its Kummer coefficients, prove that $\Phi$ is real-analytic and is the uniform limit of the rescaled profiles, that $\Phi/(\eta_1/|\eta|)$ is monotone along meridians, and that $\Phi$ is proportional to $\eta_1/|\eta|$ if and only if $2\alpha+q=1$. Every self-similar solution of finite energy, or continuous away from the origin, is dominated in absolute value by the positive one, and for $(N+4+2\alpha)/(N+2)\le q<q_c$ the only nontrivial ones are $\pm u_s$. For $\alpha=0$ existence, uniqueness and the upper bound are due to Marcus and V\'eron; the lower bound with the sharp exponent and the description of $\Phi$ are new also in that case. The existence and uniqueness proofs use a Brezis--Oswald type comparison principle and explicit barriers, given by explicit formulas; the analysis of $\Phi$ uses Kummer functions.
item.dc:creator: Waad Al Sayed, Mustapha Jazar

item.title: Dynamics of subcritical threshold solutions for the three-dimensional energy-critical NLS
item.description: arXiv:2611.09185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the radial threshold classification of Duyckaerts and Merle on the lower kinetic branch to nonradial solutions of the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in \(\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)\). At the ground state energy and with initial gradient norm strictly below that of the ground state, every solution is global and either scatters in both time directions or is a symmetry transform of the special solution \(W^-\), possibly after conjugate time reversal. The proof combines Su and Zhao's below-threshold scattering theorem with a coercivity estimate for the interaction form at threshold under a kinetic gap and a local analysis near the ground state orbit.
item.dc:creator: Meng Chen, Han Wang

item.title: Boundary singularities for the Lane-Emden equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $n\ge3$ and $(n+1)/(n-1)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct positive solutions of $\Delta u+u^p=0$ in the half-space with zero Dirichlet data away from the origin, the homogeneous singular profile there, and Poisson-kernel decay at infinity, resolving a question of del Pino--Musso--Pacard. Under a weighted non-degeneracy condition, these half-space solutions serve as building blocks for positive very weak solutions in smooth bounded domains, singular along prescribed compact smooth boundary submanifolds of normal dimension $n$. We verify non-degeneracy in the initial stable interval and at and just beyond its threshold when this lies below $(n+2)/(n-2)$. For isolated boundary singularities, the construction applies throughout the strict subcritical interval outside a locally finite exceptional set.
item.dc:creator: Weiwei Ao, Sho Katayama, Juncheng Wei

item.title: Single-scale regularity from Dirichlet energy for the five-dimensional stationary Navier--Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.09289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an interior $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion for suitable weak solutions of the unforced stationary Navier--Stokes equations in an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^5$. There exists a universal constant $\varepsilon_\ast>0$ such that $x_0$ is regular if, for some ball $B_R(x_0)\subset\Omega$ with $R>0$, \[ \frac1R\int_{B_R(x_0)}|\nabla u|^2\,dx \leq \varepsilon_\ast^2. \] The main difficulty is that the Dirichlet energy controls the velocity oscillation while its mean may be arbitrarily large. Subtracting the mean introduces a large constant drift into the perturbation equation. Moreover, smallness in $H^1$ alone is insufficient to close a direct nonlinear elliptic estimate in five dimensions. We overcome these difficulties through uniform Oseen estimates and a relative-energy comparison yielding quadratic improvement of the perturbation. As a consequence, the singular set has zero one-dimensional upper Minkowski content on every compact subset of $\Omega$, and hence local upper Minkowski dimension at most one.
item.dc:creator: Shuai Li, Jianbo Yu

item.title: Kolmogorov Obstacle Problems: Euclidean Free Boundary Regularity under a Cone Condition
item.description: arXiv:2611.09428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study obstacle problems for Kolmogorov-type operators that diffuse in one variable and transport in another. Such problems describe American options on running averages. Under a cone estimate, a strong monotonicity condition on the solution in the diffusive direction, we show that the free boundary is a graph in the diffusive direction with H\"older continuous first derivatives in the Euclidean sense, and that every free boundary point is regular. The key observation is that a Euclidean Lipschitz free boundary is flat at the intrinsic scale. For the American fixed-strike Asian option we verify the cone estimate, so that its exercise boundary has the same regularity.
item.dc:creator: Junkee Jeon, Takwon Kim, Jehan Oh

item.title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions to the critical $p$-Laplace equation near isolated singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.09440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of weak solutions to the following critical $p$-Laplace equation \[ -\Delta_p u=u^{p^*-1}, \quad u\ge0 \quad\hbox{in }B_1\setminus\{0\}, \] where $\Delta_pu=\diver(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u)$ is the classical $p$-Laplacian with $1<p<n$, $p^*=\frac{np}{n-p}$ is the Sobolev critical exponent and $B_1\setminus\{0\}\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is the punctured unit ball. We develop a nonlinear potential-theoretic method to establish sharp upper bounds for solutions, without using the method of moving planes or moving spheres. Furthermore, we use Steiner symmetrization to study the radial symmetry of global singular solutions, and thereby classify all Fowler singular solutions. Finally, we prove that every local singular solution is asymptotic to a global Fowler singular solution.
item.dc:creator: Hui Yang

item.title: Isolated yet highly unstable 2D Euler equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2611.09444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct steady solutions of the two-dimensional Euler equations on smooth annular domains that are isolated, modulo scaling, in the $L^\infty$ vorticity topology. They are highly unstable: any Yudovich trajectory remaining sufficiently close to such an equilibrium on an open time interval is a stationary multiple of it and, moreover, at fixed energy, enstrophy and circulations, distinct nearby trajectories cannot return even weakly to the equilibrium. Further, on any non-circular annulus, we show that this kind of isolated, highly unstable equilibria occurs arbitrarily close in the Yudovich norm to smooth equilibria which are themselves non-isolated.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Enciso, Antonio J. Fern\'andez, Marc Nualart

item.title: Well-posedness of weak solutions for the time-dependent thermal-fluid-solid multiphysical coupled model
item.description: arXiv:2611.09482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper constructs a time-dependent thermal-fluid-solid multiphysical coupled model describing the interaction between a free fluid and a thermo-poroelastic medium and provides a rigorous mathematical analysis. The model consists of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations and the heat equation in the free-fluid region, together with the thermo-poroelasticity equations in the porous medium. The two regions are coupled on a fixed interface through conditions for normal velocity, tangential velocity, stress balance, temperature continuity, and heat flux continuity. Under a small-data assumption, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a weak solution for this fully dynamic nonlinear coupled system. The proof employs the Galerkin method to construct semi-discrete approximations, establishes uniform a priori estimates that enable the extension of local solutions to global ones, and invokes compactness arguments to pass to the limit, yielding a solution to the original coupled system.
item.dc:creator: Yi Qin, Siyu Yang, Luling Cao, Jian Li

item.title: Nonlinear stability of planar contact waves for the 3-D compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the whole space
item.description: arXiv:2611.09485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the global nonlinear stability of small planar contact waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\R^3$ under general $H^4(\R^3)$ perturbations, without any $L^1$ integrability or zero-mass assumptions. Unlike the one-dimensional problem or the periodic channel, the problem in $\R^3$ admits neither a Poincar\'e inequality in the transverse directions nor a square-integrable anti-derivative. Our proof relies on three main ingredients: a perturbation around the one-dimensional Navier--Stokes solution starting from the smooth contact profile, a formulation of the low-order perturbation system in the velocity, pressure, and entropy variables with separate estimates for the velocity--pressure pair and the entropy, and the construction of characteristic and space-time Gaussian weight functions. Combining these weighted estimates with higher-order derivative bounds and homogeneous Gagliardo--Nirenberg interpolation yields global stability and algebraic $L^\infty$ decay rates in $\R^3$.
item.dc:creator: Feimin Huang, Rui Li, Xiaochun Wu, Lingda Xu

item.title: Sharper energy scaling bounds of the singularly perturbed Tartar square
item.description: arXiv:2611.09500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we discuss the scaling behaviour of the singularly perturbed Tartar square, revisiting the results by [R\"uland-Tribuzio '22]. Therein, it was proven that both lower and upper bounds satisfy a behaviour of the same type, up to a small mismatch of logarithmic powers. We show by an improvement of the ansatz free lower bound that the logarithmic powers indeed match and that the bounds are of order $\exp( - C \log(\varepsilon^{-1})^{1/2} )$ for suitable constants $C = C_{\rm low}$ and $C = C_{\rm upp}$, where $\varepsilon$ denotes the singular perturbation parameter. More specifically, the bootstrap argument in the Fourier space is refined by resorting to Fourier multipliers enjoying $L^\infty$-bounds which are constructed via de la Vall\'ee Poussin kernels. Regarding upper bounds, we perform iterated branching constructions sharpening the upper bound of [Winter '97] which resorted to an iteration of laminates as a competitor. Eventually, the mismatch of upper and lower bound is quantified, and for quadratic energies we obtain the bounds $C_{\rm low} \leq 7.0339$ and $C_{\rm upp} \geq 2 \log(2) - \nu $ for any $\nu>0$.
item.dc:creator: Lennart Machill

item.title: Angular Besov Refinement of the Spherical Stein--Tomas Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.09507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spherical Stein--Tomas inequality maps $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$ into $L^4(\mathbb R^3)$. We study its refinement in which the angular input is measured by the strictly weaker Besov norm $B^0_{2,4}(\mathbb S^2)$. The central separated-band inequality bounds the squared $L^2$ norm of the product of extensions from degrees $L\ll K$ by $C(L/K)$ times the squared input norms. An exact spherical-Hankel expansion controls the far field, while angular-momentum leakage and transversality handle the Fresnel region. We construct scale-separated, normalized angular bands for which the extension norm is equivalent to the $\ell^4$ norm of the coefficients. This proves that the fourth-power summation is optimal and quantitatively distinguishes the result from the classical $\ell^2$ summation. As an application, small angular Besov data generate small $L^4$ solutions to the cubic nonlinear Helmholtz equation in $\mathbb R^3$, with a smallness condition that remains sharp on multiscale data even when their $L^2$ norm is arbitrarily large or infinite. The associated on-shell nonlinear scattering amplitude has improved angular $B^0_{2,4/3}$ regularity, and its leading cubic term is quantitatively decoupled across widely separated angular bands.
item.dc:creator: R. Shahmurov, V. Shahmurov

item.title: The BCC lattice is the optimal 3D lattice quantizer for all $p\geq1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every finite $p\ge1$, the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the $p$th moment of the Voronoi cell among three-dimensional lattices of covolume one, up to orthogonal transformations. This proves the Graf--Luschgy conjecture for three-dimensional lattice quantizers (\cite{GL}).
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo

item.title: Regularity of planar Griffith minimizers with connected cracks through a monotonicity formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.09562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a new monotonicity formula for the two-dimensional Neumann elasticity equation with connected boundary. From this we deduce a regularity result for two-dimensional minimizers of the Griffith energy with connected crack set: the crack may be partitioned into regular points, triple junctions, and cracktips. We give a classification of the global minimizers of the Griffith energy with connected crack set. Finally, we discuss some consequences of the monotonicity formula on the evolution of the stress intensity factors along a crack, which may present independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Camille Labourie, Antoine Lemenant, Micka\"el Nahon

item.title: Generalized and Classical Harnack Inequalities for semilinear equations on Carnot Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.09590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove generalized and classical Harnack inequalities for non-negative smooth solutions of divergence-form semilinear subelliptic equations on Carnot groups. The proof combines smooth horizontal Gauss--Green and coarea formulas, energy estimates for level sets, a Vitali covering argument, and a horizontal Keller--Osserman barrier. The companion paper, Reference [10], develops the geometric foundations and extends the estimates to weak solutions with nonsmooth data.
item.dc:creator: Cristian E. Guti\'errez, Ahmed Mohammed

item.title: The variational formulation of the follow-the-leader model
item.description: arXiv:2611.09781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a variational formulation of a finite-dimensional Follow-the-Leader system through a minimizing-movement scheme based on a discrete transport distance with nonlinear mobility. Despite the degeneracy of the kinetic action at maximal density, we prove finiteness of the distance, $C^1$ regularity of geodesics, and suitable Euler--Lagrange relations. For a decreasing external potential, we show that the JKO scheme yields an approximate implicit Euler discretization of the Follow-the-Leader dynamics. Consequently, as $\tau\to0^+$, the piecewise affine interpolations converge, up to a subsequence, to a $C^1$ solution of the continuous Follow-the-Leader system. This complements the many-particle convergence theory for the discrete nonlinear-mobility transport distance by establishing the continuous-time limit at fixed number of particles.
item.dc:creator: Maicol Caponi, Marco Di Francesco, Emanuela Radici

item.title: On the Principal Eigenvalue of the $(p,A)$-Laplacian with Sign-Changing Morrey Potentials: Complete Continuity, Optimization, and Differentiability
item.description: arXiv:2611.09793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a unified framework to study the continuity and complete continuity of the principal eigenvalue functional $\lambda_1(V,m)$ associated with the following $(p,A)$-Laplacian operator involving both sign-changing potential $V$, and positive weight $m$ in a Morrey space: \begin{align*} -\Delta_{p,A}(u) + V|u|^{p-2}u &= \lambda m|u|^{p-2}u \quad \text{in}\,\, \Omega, u &= 0 \quad\quad\quad \quad\quad \text{on}\,\, \partial\Omega, \end{align*} where $1<p<N$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ is a parameter, and $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N (N \geq 2)$ is a bounded domain with boundary $\partial \Omega$. As a consequence, we investigate the existence and uniqueness of optimal principal eigenvalues $\lambda_1(V,m)$ over a weakly compact subset of the Morrey space. Finally, we derive a formula for the derivative of $\lambda_1(V,m)$ with respect to regular perturbations of potential $V$, and positive weight $m$ within a closed subspace of Morrey space. Our results develop analytic tools to overcome the lack of separability and reflexivity in Morrey spaces to investigate this eigenvalue problem. In particular, the study is new even for the linear case $p=2$. We also emphasize that the tools established are applicable for a wide class of PDEs with coefficients in Morrey spaces.
item.dc:creator: Pradeep Gupta, Ratan Kr. Giri, Sekhar Ghosh

item.title: Large-Time Behavior and Asymptotic Profiles for Time-Fractional Nonlinear Diffusion Equations via Entropy Methods
item.description: arXiv:2611.09858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the large-time behavior of nonnegative solutions to the time-fractional nonlinear diffusion equation $\partial_t^{\alpha}(u-u_0) = \Delta u^m$, $0<\alpha<1$, $m>0$, in a bounded domain with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that the rescaled solution $t^{\frac{\alpha}{m}}u$ converges as $t\to\infty$ to an asymptotic profile $S$ characterized by $-\Delta S^m = u_0/\Gamma(1-\alpha)$. Moreover, we show that $t^\alpha u^m$ converges to $S^m$, which admits an explicit representation in terms of the Green function and the initial datum. In contrast to the classical case $\alpha=1$, the asymptotic profile depends explicitly on the initial datum.
item.dc:creator: Mikiya Kametaka

item.title: Unconditional Uniqueness of KdV and mKdV Green Solutions at Low Regularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.09885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove unconditional uniqueness for the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation in $C_tH^{-1}_x(\mathbb R)$ and the real defocusing modified KdV equation in $C_tL^2_x(\mathbb R)$ within the class of Green solutions, an intrinsically well defined solution notion that encodes the evolution at these low regularities through the diagonal Green functions of the associated Lax operators. A key contribution is automatic local smoothing: the Green identities imply $q\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for KdV and $u_x,u^2\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for mKdV in spacetime, with estimates uniform over spatial translates. The uniqueness results therefore identify every Green solution in these classes with the continuous extension of the corresponding Schwartz flow.
item.dc:creator: Zhimeng Ouyang

item.title: Gaussian fluctuations of the moderately interacting Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto particle system around the mollified mean-field limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.08601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study, at the logarithmic mollification scale $\eta^{-2(d+1+\alpha)}\le\delta\log N$ of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{\"u}ngel, the fluctuation field $V^N=\sqrt N(\mu^N-u_\eta)$ of the moderately interacting multi-species particle system whose mean-field limit is the Shigesada- Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system. The field is centred at the solution $u_\eta$ of the mollified equation, which depends on $N$ through $\eta$. On a scale of weighted Bessel-potential spaces of negative order we prove that the laws of $(V^N,M^N)$ are tight, where $M^N$ is the martingale part. Every limit point of $M^N$ is a continuous Gaussian martingale with an explicit deterministic bracket. Every limit point of $V^N$ is a weak solution, and the mild solution, of a linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck SPDE whose drift is the linearisation of the SKT operator at the limit $u$. The initial field and the martingale are independent, and weak solutions are unique given both, so the whole sequence converges in law, jointly with the martingale part, and the limit is unique in law among solutions of the martingale problem. The noise is $d M_i=div(\sqrt{2u_i\Theta_i}dW_i)$, with $\Theta_i=\sigma_i+\sum_jf(a_{ij}u_j)$ and $W$ a cylindrical Wiener process on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^{nd})$. The hypotheses are those of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{\"u}ngel, including the smallness and the nonnegativity on $\mathbb{R}$ of the nonlinearity $f$. We add radial kernels $B_{ij}$, the independence of the initial data and the Brownian motions across particles and species, a smaller $\delta$, a regularity budget on $u_0$, a strengthened smallness condition on $f$ that makes the backward system diagonally dominant in weighted spaces, and an integer Sobolev index $s$.
item.dc:creator: Florian Huber

item.title: A new characterization of the round sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.08751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide an elementary proof of Hersch's inequality and Cheng's theorem, both characterizing the sphere. We revisit these classical results in connection with the geodesic monotonicity of heat kernels on two-dimensional spheres, which provides a third characterization.
item.dc:creator: Almut Burchard, \'Angel D. Mart\'inez

item.title: Boundary integral methods and shape reconstruction for periodic fluid--solid interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.09201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies direct scattering by periodic fluid--solid interfaces and interface reconstruction from multifrequency near-field data. Using Helmholtz decomposition and quasi-periodic single-layer potentials, we formulate a coupled boundary integral system with the standard stress traction, establish its equivalence to the original fluid--solid transmission problem under suitable assumptions, and construct a corresponding Nystr\"om discretization. For near-field observations at finitely many measurement points, we establish local Fr\'echet differentiability of the observation map with a quadratic remainder estimate. In the smooth setting, the derivative transmission problem and its boundary integral formulation are used to compute the observation Jacobian required for interface reconstruction. The interface is reconstructed by regularized Gauss--Newton iteration in a Fourier space that is progressively enriched as the frequency increases. Numerical experiments assess direct-solver accuracy and reconstruction performance for different interfaces, material configurations, and noise levels.
item.dc:creator: Yongxin Liu, Junliang Lv, Ning Wang, Yi Wang

item.title: Trace and Regularized Index of Callias Operators on Hyperbolic Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.09438v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $d \geq 3$ be odd. On hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$, we consider Callias-type operators, i.e. Dirac-Schr\"odinger operators of the form $D = ic \nabla + A$, where $c \nabla$ is the Dirac operator and $A$ a function with values in the self-adjoint operators, and provide an explicit formula for the iterated trace $\text{tr}_{L^2(\mathbb{H}^d,H)} \text{tr}_{S}( e^{-tD^*D} - e^{-tDD^*})$, $t>0$, that appears in the formulation of the Witten index. Thereby, the operator $D$ is not assumed to be Fredholm.
item.dc:creator: Jilly Kevo

item.title: Sharp isoperimetry in groups of polynomial growth
item.description: arXiv:2611.09443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study weighted edge boundary and outer vertex boundary on Cayley graphs of polynomial growth of degree $Q>1$. For every finite symmetric generating set, we prove that each exact isoperimetric profile satisfies $I(n)=c n^{(Q-1)/Q}+O(n^{(Q-1)/Q-\beta})$, where $\beta=1/(8Q^2)$. We identify the leading constant with the isoperimetric constant of a horizontal perimeter on the limiting Carnot group, after accounting for the counting density. Its integrand is a norm with polyhedral unit ball, determined by a convex minimization with one real variable for each coset of a torsion-free nilpotent subgroup. For every asymptotically minimizing sequence, we translate its vertex sets so that the characteristic functions of the associated rescaled regions are precompact in $L^1$. The limiting regions minimize continuum perimeter at fixed volume. The exact-cardinality estimate requires no regularity assumption on these regions. For virtually abelian groups, we prove a quantitative stability estimate using a discrete approximation to the Euclidean Wulff body. The relative symmetric difference from a translate is bounded by the square root of the sum of the relative boundary deficit and a cardinality error. We also characterize when bounded additive changes of Cayley metric preserve the leading vertex constant. Failure occurs already in rank two; we construct pairs with the same measured asymptotic cone whose leading constants have an unbounded ratio as the rank grows.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee

item.title: Finding geometric criteria for negative eigenvalues of the Neumann--Poincar\'e operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.09739v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by a question of Grigori Rozenblum, we study how the geometry of the boundary of a convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ affects whether the Neumann--Poincar\'e operator on $\partial\Omega$ has negative eigenvalues. First, we show that a flat face on the boundary of a bounded, convex Lipschitz domain produces an infinite-dimensional negative spectral subspace. For convex domains with $C^{1,\alpha}$ boundary, we bound the number of negative eigenvalues from below by the Dirichlet eigenvalue counting function of a projected patch over which the chords are sufficiently short. A Rellich identity gives a sufficient condition on a defining function to exclude negative eigenvalues. We also report numerical computations, which led us to the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Magnus Goffeng, Johan Helsing, Mikael Sundqvist

item.title: Radial reductions of variable exponent Laplacian equations on warped products with compact symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.09826v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study nonlinear elliptic equations of variable exponent type, \[ -\Delta_{q(x)}u+|u|^{q(x)-2}u=f(x,u), \] on non-compact Riemannian manifolds with symmetry. We consider complete warped products \[ M=\mathcal R\times_\phi Y,\qquad g_\phi=dr^2\oplus\phi(r)^2g_Y, \] where $\mathcal R$ is a non-compact interval, possibly with boundary, and $Y$ is a compact homogeneous manifold. We establish sufficient conditions on the warping function ensuring a Ricci lower bound, a uniform non-collapsing volume condition, and the orbit-growth hypothesis of the abstract existence theorem proved in \cite{JFA}. We also obtain comparison bounds for the admissible warping functions. We analyze the corresponding radial equations for the admissible exponential and linear models $\phi(r)=e^{ar}$ and $\phi(r)=ar$, with $r\geq r_0>0$. For a constant diffusion exponent $q=k$, we consider explicit decaying profiles $u=\phi^{-\sigma}$, which belong to $L_1^k(M)$ provided $\sigma k>\dim Y$ in the exponential case and $\sigma k>\dim Y+1$ in the linear case. Under additional explicit parameter restrictions, these profiles solve a resonant equation with a positive bounded coefficient, a construction distinct from the superlinear regime of the abstract existence theorem. Finally, we establish logarithmic reductions for constant and variable radial exponents, and justify the passage from radial identities to weak formulations against arbitrary compactly supported interior test functions.
item.dc:creator: Jose Luis Diaz Palencia, Daniel J. Pons, Enrique G. Reyes

item.title: Mass-lumped finite elements with maximum-bound preservation and original-energy dissipation for the degenerate-mobility Allen-Cahn equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09832v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we propose a mass-lumped finite element method for the Allen-Cahn equation that incorporates nonlinear mobility which may degenerate. The spatial approximation uses continuous, piecewise linear, mass-lumped finite elements, while convex splitting is employed for the double-well potential in time. Under the standard non-obtuse mesh condition, it is shown that the resulting fully discrete method preserves the maximum-bound principle unconditionally: if the initial approximation takes values in $[-1, 1]$, then so does the numerical solution at every time level. Additionally, the method dissipates the original discrete Ginzburg-Landau energy without any time-step restriction, even when the mobility vanishes at pure phases. This analysis relies on the monotonicity of the lumped finite element operator and the convexity of the split potential. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties and demonstrate the robustness of the method in phase-separation dynamics involving degenerate mobility.
item.dc:creator: Himanshu Kumar Dwivedi, Matthias Ehrhardt

item.title: Global Two-Sided Estimates for Time-Fractional Diffusion Kernels on Hyperbolic Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.09890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study time-fractional diffusion on real hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$, $n\ge2$, with Caputo order $0<\alpha<1$. We establish global two-sided pointwise estimates for the homogeneous fundamental kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$ and the inhomogeneous (Duhamel) kernel $Y_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$, uniformly over all $t>0$ and positive geodesic distances $r$. By combining inverse-stable subordination with global bounds for the hyperbolic heat kernel, we distinguish a short-time local regime, a large-time interior region, and an exterior region governed by a saddle-point problem with parameter $r/t$. Both kernels have the same exterior exponential rate, while their amplitudes are related by an explicit saddle-point factor. The estimates are uniformly comparable on the interfaces between regimes, recover the Euclidean time-fractional singularities at small scales, and identify the influence of hyperbolic geometry on large-scale decay. The kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}$ also describes the one-time marginal density of hyperbolic Brownian motion under an independent inverse stable clock. This representation yields a radial limit law, moment and quantile asymptotics, and a change in the mean square displacement from order $t^\alpha$ at small times to order $t^{2\alpha}$ at large times.
item.dc:creator: Vicente Vergara

item.title: Convergence of iterated restricted mean values to harmonic functions
item.description: arXiv:0709.3311v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain and let $\delta$ be a continuous positive function on $\Omega$ with $B(x,\delta(x))\subseteq\Omega$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $\sigma(f)(x)$ denote the average of $f$ over the ball $B(x,\delta(x))$. Restricted mean value theorems give conditions under which a fixed point of $\sigma$ must be harmonic. We study the dynamical counterpart of this question: the behavior of the iterates $\sigma^k(f)$. We show that for \emph{every} bounded domain and every bounded measurable $f$ that is continuous at the points of $\partial\Omega$, the iterates $\sigma^k(f)$ converge locally uniformly in $\Omega$ to the Perron--Wiener--Brelot solution of the Dirichlet problem with boundary values $f|_{\partial\Omega}$, and that the convergence is uniform on $\overline\Omega$ for all continuous $f$ if and only if $\Omega$ is regular for the Dirichlet problem. This contains and extends earlier results for $C^{2,\alpha}$ domains with $C^{2,\alpha}$ data and for strictly convex domains with continuous data. We also give explicit rates of convergence: an algebraic rate $O(1/k)$ on domains with a uniform exterior ball condition and a geometric rate on convex domains, when $\delta$ is comparable to the distance to the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: On the regularity of entropy solutions to stochastic degenerate parabolic equations
item.description: arXiv:2504.01794v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the regularity of entropy solutions for quasilinear parabolic equations with anisotropic degeneracy and stochastic forcing. Building on previous works, we establish space-time regularity under a non-degeneracy condition that does not require an assumption on the derivative of the symbol of the corresponding kinetic equation, a restriction imposed in earlier studies. This allows us to obtain regularity results for certain equations not accounted for by prior theory, albeit with reduced regularity exponents. Our approach uses a kinetic formulation with two transport equations, one of second order and one of first order, leveraging a form of "parabolic regularity" inherent in these equations that was not utilized in previous studies.
item.dc:creator: Marko Erceg, Kenneth H. Karlsen, Darko Mitrovi\'c

item.title: Exponential Decays of Steklov Eigenfunctions for the Magnetic Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2511.14054v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\beta$ associated with the Schr\"odinger operator $(D+\beta \A)^2$ with a magnetic potential in a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega$, where $\beta>1$ is the field strength parameter. Assume that the magnetic field $\B=\nabla \times \A$ is of finite type. We show that if $\beta>\beta_0$, the ground state for $\Lambda_\beta$ decays exponentially away from a neighborhood of the subset of $\partial\Omega$, on which $\B$ vanishes to the maximal order.
item.dc:creator: Zhongwei Shen

item.title: Sharp Convergence to the Half-Space for Mullins-Sekerka in the Plane
item.description: arXiv:2511.23270v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit the HED Method for the Mullins-Sekerka evolution in the plane. We identify a natural notion of distance, intrinsic to the interface itself. Using this distance, the energy, and the dissipation, we develop natural assumptions on the flow and, assuming existence of a solution satisfying these conditions, obtain not just the algebraic rate (already previously derived by Chugreeva, Otto, and M.G. Westdickenberg) but also the sharp leading order constant for the convergence to the flat limiting interface. To carry this out, we introduce a lemma that obtains optimal algebraic decay behavior (rate and prefactor) from given variational information.
item.dc:creator: Wenhui Shi, Maria G. Westdickenberg, Michael Westdickenberg

item.title: Regularity for fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with strong absorption
item.description: arXiv:2512.08196v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate dead-core problems for fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with strong absorption, \begin{equation*} |Du|^{p} F(D^{2}u) - u_{t} = \lambda_{0}(x,t)\, u^{\mu}\, \chi_{\{u>0\}}(x,t) \qquad \text{in } \quad \Omega_{T} := \Omega \times (0,T), \end{equation*} where $0\le p<\infty$, $0<\mu<1$ and $u \geq 0 $ is a bounded viscosity solution satisfying $0\le u_t\le A_0u^\mu$ in the viscosity sense for some $0\le A_0<\infty$. We establish a sharp and improved parabolic $C^{\alpha}$-regularity estimate along the free boundary $\partial \{ u > 0 \}$, where \[ \alpha := \frac{2+p}{1+p-\mu} > 1 + \frac{1}{1+p}. \] Moreover, we establish weak geometric properties of solutions, such as non-degeneracy and uniform positive density. As an application, we obtain a Liouville-type theorem for entire solutions and gradient bounds. Finally, as a byproduct of our approach, we derive a new formulation of the gradient decay property and establish a Harnack-type inequality on time slices. It is worth noting that the results presented here extend those in da Silva {\em et al.}(Pacific J. Math., \textbf{300} (2019), 179--213) and (J. Differential Equations., \textbf{264} (2018), 7270--7293) to the degenerate setting, and can be viewed as a parabolic analogue of da Silva {\em et al.} (Math. Nachr., \textbf{294} (2021), 38--55) and Teixeira (Math. Ann., \textbf{364} (2016), 1121--1134).
item.dc:creator: Jiangwen Wang, Jo\~ao Vitor da Silva, Feida Jiang

item.title: DeepRitzSplit: A Variational Neural Operator Framework for Gradient Flows with Application to Dendritic Growth
item.description: arXiv:2604.18261v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Phase-field models are widely used to simulate microstructure evolution but their numerical solution remains computationally demanding. Neural operator surrogates provide a promising alternative, yet existing approaches are data-driven, requiring large datasets and exhibiting limited robustness when extrapolating to unseen configurations. We introduce DeepRitzSplit, an unsupervised neural operator framework for gradient-flow systems based on a variational formulation of energy-stable splitting schemes. It learns the time evolution semigroup associated with a convex-concave free-energy decomposition by minimizing the underlying variational problem at each time step. It is designed to inherit the dissipative structure of the underlying gradient flow without requiring trajectory datasets. We further introduce a Reaction-Diffusion Neural Operator (RDNO) architecture motivated by splitting schemes, with separate reaction and diffusion components to improve training efficiency and interpretability. We assess the approach on the Allen-Cahn equation and apply it to a phase-field model of anisotropic dendritic growth during solidification. In the Allen-Cahn benchmark, DeepRitzSplit shows better generalization than the supervised baseline on the out-of-distribution configurations tested, using 180 training configurations. In dendritic growth, the method captures the overall phase morphology and dendrite tip velocity well, while the tip radius is more sensitive to the training strategy. Refinement based on the residual of the splitting scheme markedly improves this second-order morphological quantity. The trained operators retain good predictive capabilities on configurations substantially different from the training set. These results demonstrate the potential of variationally trained neural operators as physically informed surrogates for accelerated microstructure simulations.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Appolaire, Ludovick Gagnon, Chih-Kang Huang, Miha Zalo\v{z}nik

item.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
item.description: arXiv:2604.18540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.
item.dc:creator: Leon Bungert, Lucas Schmitt

item.title: A generalisation of the Gagliardo--Nirenberg Inequality with applications to mass-critical and mass-subcritical elliptic equations
item.description: arXiv:2604.24381v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Via a new inequality \`a la Gagliardo--Nirenberg, we prove the existence and nonexistence of solutions to \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} (-\Delta)^s u + \frac{\mu}{|y|^{2s}} u + \lambda u = f(u), \quad \mathbb{R}^N \ni x = (y,z) \in \mathbb{R}^K \times \mathbb{R}^{N-K}, \\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} u^2 \, \mathrm{d}x = \rho \end{cases} \end{equation*} in the mass-critical and mass-subcritical regimes, where $s>0$, $N \ge K \ge 2$, $\mu \in \mathbb{R}$ belongs to a specific range, $\rho>0$ is given a priori, and $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$ is unknown. Additionally, we obtain similar results for the problem above with $\mu=0$ and $N \ge 1$ as well as a related curl-curl equation. Finally, we provide a thorough insight into the threshold for $\rho$ that divides the scenarios of negative and zero least energy.
item.dc:creator: Bartosz Bieganowski, Jacopo Schino

item.title: Resolvent Estimates for the Stokes Operator in a Three-Dimensional Lipschitz Domain
item.description: arXiv:2609.02552v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By refining the approach developed in \cite{AGH-2015, GS2026a}, we establish resolvent estimates in $L^p_\sigma (\Omega)$ for the Stokes operator in a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega$ in $\R^3$ for $(3/2)-\e< p\le \infty$, where $\e>0$ depends on $\Omega$. As a consequence, the Stokes operator generates a uniformly bounded analytic semigroup in $L^p_\sigma (\Omega)$. The range for $p$ is sharp. The results are particularly surprising, as it is long believed that the $L^p$ resolvent estimates in three-dimensional Lipschitz domains may fail for large $p$. In the appendices we prove an interpolation theorem between $L^2_\sigma(\Omega)$ and $L^\infty_\sigma(\Omega)$. We also show that for $1< p< \infty$ and a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega$ in $\R^d, d\ge 2$, the resolvent estimate in $L^p(\Omega; \C^d)$ can hold only if the Helmholtz projection is bounded on this space. This explains the counter-example constructed in \cite{Deuring-2001}. Finally, we prove that the resolvent estimate may fail in $L^p_\sigma (\Omega)$ for $1< p< (3/2)$ and $d\ge 3$ as a consequence of failure of the Helmholtz decomposition of $L^p(\Omega; \C^d)$.
item.dc:creator: Zhongwei Shen

item.title: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range
item.description: arXiv:2609.40068v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the present paper, we extend the results in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen from the slowly rotating regime $|a|\ll m$ to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The restriction $|a|\ll m$ enters in fact only through the estimates for wave equations and for the Bianchi system established in \cite{GKS22}. To remove this restriction, we crucially rely on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. Additionally, some of the results of the present paper are proved in our companion paper \cite{Sze}.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\'emie Szeftel

item.title: Teukolsky equations in perturbations of Kerr
item.description: arXiv:2609.40315v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Kerr stability conjecture has been proved in the slowly rotating case, i.e., $|a|\ll m$, in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen, and extended in \cite{Sze}, by the author, to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The proof in \cite{Sze} crucially relies on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the scalar wave equation and for Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. In addition, two results in \cite{Sze}, concerning the derivation of the Teukolsky wave-transport system in perturbations of Kerr and energy-Morawetz estimates for Teukolsky in the setting of \cite{Sze}, are stated without proofs. The goal of the present paper companion paper to \cite{Sze} is to provide the proof of these two results.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\'emie Szeftel

item.title: Boundary-layer separation beyond the square-root law
item.description: arXiv:2610.01689v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct solutions to the two-dimensional stationary Prandtl system under a constant adverse pressure gradient exhibiting a family of distinct separation laws. More precisely, for every integer $\ell\ge1$, we construct smooth initial data for which separation occurs at a finite location $x=x^\ast$, with \[ \partial_y u(x,0) =\mathbf C_\ell(x^\ast-x)^{\ell/2}\bigl(1+o(1)\bigr), \qquad x\uparrow x^\ast, \] where $\mathbf C_\ell>0$ depends on the initial data. We determine the local asymptotic structure of the solution near separation through matched inner and outer expansions based on linearization around the ground state in von Mises variables. This description addresses Open Problem~5 proposed by Oleinik and Samokhin~\cite{OleinikSamok-book-99}. We prove the nonlinear stability of the square-root separation law ($\ell=1$) under small admissible perturbations of the initial data in a suitable topology.
item.dc:creator: Ky Giao Duong, Tej-Eddine Ghoul, Sameer Iyer, Yasunori Maekawa

item.title: Logarithmic upper bounds and axial front selection for spatially periodic lattice Fisher--KPP equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.06381v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t=\Delta_{\Z^d}u+F(x,u)$ on $\Z^d$ ($d\geq2$) with a spatially periodic Fisher--KPP reaction $F$ and a nonzero, finitely supported initial datum $u_0:\Z^d\to[0,1]$. We establish a logarithmic upper bound on the front position that holds uniformly in the observation direction, with a logarithmic delay coefficient governed by the outward normal to the asymptotic spreading body. When the linearized growth rate $F_s(x,0)$ is independent of the longitudinal coordinate, we prove the matching axial Bramson correction and show that the solution converges uniformly on fixed-width half-tubes to a critical pulsating front up to a bounded, slowly varying phase shift. For critical pulsating profiles $\Phi(s,x)$ satisfying $\Phi(s,x)\leq C(1+s)\ee^{-\lambda s}$ for $s\geq0$ and $x\in\Z^d$, where $\lambda>0$ is the critical spatial decay rate, we derive the precise leading-edge asymptotic expansion and prove uniqueness up to translation. As a consequence, in the axial regime we obtain sharp asymptotics for the arrival times $T_\theta(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:u(t,x)\geq\theta\}$ ($0<\theta<1$), including the asymptotic time lag between distinct level sets at a remote site and the period-to-period passage time along the axis. For general periodic linearized growth rates, we introduce a nonlinear subsolution built from a positive quotient of linear Dirichlet evolutions on a retreating domain and formulate sufficient kernel estimates for a matching directional lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Yuanyang Hu, Zhenkun Wang

item.title: Seifert type magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.08519v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains whose magnetic lines define an $(m,n)$ Seifert fibration for arbitrary coprime integers $m,n$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Peralta-Salas, Radu Slobodeanu

item.title: Scattering in spacetime cones for the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.29265v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$, with a class of `mixed' nonlinearities that admit soliton solutions. We are interested in the long-time behaviour of solutions with finite, but possibly large, mass and/or energy. By a spacetime cone, we mean an open set in $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}_{x,t}$ that is invariant under dilation $(x, t) \mapsto (\alpha x, \alpha t)$ for all $\alpha > 0$. Our main result is as follows: let $u(x, t)$ be the solution with initial condition in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. Let $\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}$ be the mass and energy of $u$, and let $\eta = \eta(\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}) > 0$ be sufficiently small. Let $C_\epsilon$ be the complement of $N \geq 1$ of sufficiently thin spacetime cones $\{ (x, t) \mid |x-v_jt| \leq \epsilon t \}$, where $v_1, \dots, v_N$ are fixed velocities and $\epsilon$ is sufficiently small. If the $L^\infty$ norm of $u$ in $C_\epsilon$ is $\leq \eta$, we prove that $u$ scatters in $C_{2\epsilon} \subset C_\epsilon$.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Hassell, Qiuye Jia, Xiaoxu Wu

item.title: Self-similar solutions for the gSQG patch equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.32857v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The inviscid generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations are a family of active scalar equations parametrized by a scalar $\alpha$ that includes the two-dimensional Euler equations ($\alpha = 0)$ and the SQG equation $(\alpha = 1)$. We prove that, for every $\alpha \in (\frac{7}{4}, 2)$ and every $T > 0$, there exists a self-similar patch solution whose boundary is a smooth, unbounded graph for $0 \leq t < T$ and develops a corner singularity at time $T$. The proof has been formally verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Javier G\'omez-Serrano, Marcus Pasquariello

item.title: Bottom-boundary identification using asymptotic observers in dispersive shallow-water models
item.description: arXiv:2611.01738v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of identifying the bottom-boundary of an ocean basin, particularly in the coastal region where shallow-water theory applies. Our main contribution is the development of an easy-to-implement observer-based approach of identifying the bottom-boundary profile from measurements of the free-surface. Furthermore, we prove that the true profile can be obtained by minimising the long-time observation-error as computed from the observer equations associated with a class of linear dispersive shallow water-wave models. Numerical simulations indicate the same optimisation problem can recover the true profile for the nonlinear versions of the same dispersive water-wave models.
item.dc:creator: Vishal Neeraje, Vishal Vasan

item.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.03527v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schr\"odinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.
item.dc:creator: Yinghao Gong

item.title: Fundamental solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian in cone-like domains, with applications to Liouville-type theorems and global H\"older regularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.07157v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $ C_\omega$ be the cone generated by a proper $C^2$ domain $\omega\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$. We study positive homogeneous solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation in $C_\omega$ with zero exterior values. For $p\ne2$, the operator is nonlinear and not uniformly elliptic. For every $p>1$, we identify two extremal homogeneities $\beta^+>0>\beta^-$, prove that every fundamental solution, if one exists, has one of these exponents, and construct homogeneous eigenfunctions whose eigenvalues have signs determined by the position of the homogeneity relative to $\beta^\pm$. As an application, we obtain the Lane-Emden threshold $q^*=p-1+sp/\beta^+$ for every $p>1$: nontrivial nonnegative supersolutions of $(-\Delta_p)^s u\ge u^q$ in $C_\omega$ do not exist for $0<q<q^*$, whereas homogeneous supersolutions exist for $q>q^*$. We also establish Hopf-type lower bounds at conical boundary points with the optimal exponent. When $p-1>sp$ , we construct both fundamental solutions, one singular at the vertex and the other vanishing there. For $p=2$, these solutions are known; our method recovers them for every $s\in(0,1)$. The homogeneous eigenfunctions also serve as barriers, yielding boundary decay and global H\"older regularity for $(-\Delta_p)^s u=f$ in bounded Lipschitz domains, with zero exterior values and $f$ continuous up to the boundary. The admissible H\"older exponents are determined by the exterior cones. All results hold for every $N\ge2$; in particular, $N>sp$ is not needed.
item.dc:creator: Reshmi Biswas, Alexander Quaas

item.title: Fluctuation Correction and Global Solutions for the Stochastic Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto System via Entropy-Based Regularization
item.description: arXiv:2501.17953v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a stochastic extension of the n-species Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system, in which a multiplicative noise term accounts for fluctuation corrections to the mean-field dynamics arising from a finite underlying population. The noise we consider is motivated by, but not rigorously derived from, the particle-system approximation of Chen, Daus, Holzinger, and J"ungel; it only partially respects the entropy (gradient-flow) structure of the deterministic system, which is the main source of the technical difficulties addressed in this paper. For the resulting system of stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), we establish the existence of nonnegative, global, weak martingale solutions, under a detailed-balance condition on the diffusion coefficients and a smallness condition relating the noise intensity to these coefficients. This smallness condition amounts to a sufficiently large population size N (equivalently, small fluctuation strength 1/N): the existence theory thus operates in the perturbative regime around the deterministic mean-field limit, and for fixed coefficients it is always satisfiable once N is large enough.
item.dc:creator: Florian Huber

item.title: A structure and asymptotic preserving scheme for the quasineutral limit of the Vlasov-Poisson system
item.description: arXiv:2504.04826v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we propose a new numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system that is both asymptotically consistent and stable in the quasineutral regime, i.e. when the Debye length $\lambda$ is small compared to the characteristic spatial scale of the physical domain. Our approach consists in reformulating the Vlasov-Poisson system as a hyperbolic problem by applying a spectral expansion in the basis of Hermite functions in the velocity space and in designing a structure-preserving scheme for the time and spatial variables. Through this Hermite formulation, we establish a convergence result for the electric field toward its quasineutral limit together with explicit error estimates in $\lambda$. Following this path, we then propose a fully discrete numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system, inspired by the approach in arXiv:2306.14605, and rigorously prove that it is uniformly consistent in the quasineutral limit regime. Finally, we present several numerical simulations to illustrate the behavior of the proposed scheme. These results demonstrate the capability of our method to describe quasineutral plasmas, illustrate its stability and confirm its asymptotic preserving property.
