item.title: Free energy Wasserstein gradient flow and their particle counterparts: toy model, (degenerate) PL inequalities and exit times
item.description: arXiv:2510.16506v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In finite dimension, the long-time and metastable behavior of a gradient flow perturbated by a small Brownian noise is well understood. A similar situation arises when a Wasserstein gradient flow over a space of probability measure is approximated by a system of mean-field interacting particles, but classical results do not apply in these infinite-dimensional settings. We are concerned with the situation where the objective function of the optimization problem contains an entropic penalization, so that the particle system is a Langevin diffusion process. The work has two parts: the first and main one is devoted to the general study of a very simple class of models, for which the infinite-dimensional behavior is fully characterized by an autonomous diffusion process at fixed finite dimension. On the one hand, we prove the equivalence between fast convergence for the mean-field gradient flow and for the particle system in terms of functional inequalities (log-Sobolev, Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz, Talagrand and variants thereof) including the degenerate polynomial case occurring at phase transitions, and on the other hand we characterise the metastable behavior in terms of transition time between local minimiser -- establishing an Eyring-Kramers formula -- and of exit time from unstable critical points. In a second part, motivated by and building on the systematic study of the toy models, we consider the continuous Curie-Weiss model in a symmetric double-well potential, exactly at the critical temperature. We show that, although the $N$-particle Gibbs measure does not satisfy a uniform-in-$N$ standard log-Sobolev inequality (the optimal constant growing like $\sqrt{N}$), it does satisfy a more general {\L}ojasiewicz inequality uniformly in $N$, inducing uniform polynomial long-time convergence rates, propagation of chaos at stationarity and uniformly in time, and creation of chaos.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Monmarch\'e

item.title: Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation
item.description: arXiv:2602.00853v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We review quantitative results on the convergence to equilibrium of the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation, $p>1$, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with additive, possibly degenerate Wiener noise. From these results we derive upper bounds on $\varepsilon$-mixing times in different distances, depending on the initial data. We show that the Wasserstein distance to equilibrium is non-increasing in time and that, for $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$, the invariant measure has moments of all orders. For $1<p<2$ with $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$ and possibly degenerate noise, the $\varepsilon$-mixing times in every Wasserstein distance $\mathcal{W}_r$, $r\ge1$, are $O(\varepsilon^{-\delta})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ for every $\delta>0$. Two tables collect the convergence rates and the mixing-time bounds.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Barrera, Jonas M. T\"olle

item.title: Smooth Piecewise Cutting for Neural Operator to Handle Discontinuities and Sharp Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2605.19823v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural operators have achieved strong performance in learning solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs), but their inherently continuous representations struggle to capture discontinuities and sharp transitions. Existing approaches typically approximate such features within continuous function spaces, often requiring increased model capacity and high-resolution data. In this work, we propose Cut-DeepONet, a two-stage training framework that explicitly models discontinuities while reducing learning complexity. Our approach reformulates the problem via a lifting strategy, partitioning the domain into smooth subregions while representing discontinuities as boundaries in a higher-dimensional space. This separation aligns the operator learning task with the inductive bias of neural networks and avoids directly approximating discontinuities. An additional network predicts input-dependent discontinuity locations for unseen inputs, which are then used to guide the neural operator in generating smooth components within each region. Experiments on benchmark PDEs show that Cut-DeepONet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, even when trained on low-resolution datasets. The method excels on problems with discontinuities and sharp transitions, while using fewer trainable parameters. Our results highlight the benefits of changing the representation of operator learning rather than increasing model complexity.
item.dc:creator: Ha Dang, Sebastian Schmidt, Juergen Hesser

item.title: Local conservation laws, symmetries and Hamiltonian structure of three-dimensional incompressible Euler flow
item.description: arXiv:2609.23772v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: All smooth local conservation laws, symmetries and adjoint symmetries of three-dimensional homogeneous incompressible Euler flow are classified in the primitive velocity--pressure variables. Explicit dependence on time and position and arbitrary finite orders of mixed time and spatial derivatives are allowed. Up to trivial currents, the conservation laws consist of incompressibility, linear and angular momentum, kinetic energy, helicity and generalised time-dependent momentum. Every local adjoint symmetry is represented by a multiplier of these currents. Every finite-order local symmetry is equivalent on solutions to a classical point symmetry, resolving a conjecture of Olver. An explicit local first-order Hamiltonian structure of the primitive system is also established in the geometric theory of partial differential equations. It maps the energy multiplier to time translation; its kernel on local adjoint symmetries is spanned by the helicity and incompressibility multipliers. The proof first excludes higher-order symmetries by comparing their responses to transverse and harmonic characteristic directions in compatible derivative data. The Hamiltonian map and its kernel then determine all local adjoint symmetries from the symmetry classification. Exact multiplier identities and the correspondence between multipliers and current classes complete the conservation-law classification.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Shevyakov

item.title: Feynman-Kac Representation and the Asymptotic Speed of the Fisher-KPP Equation with Finite-Activity Jump Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.07868v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic propagation speed of travelling wave solutions to the stochastic Fisher--KPP equation with multiplicative finite-activity pure jump L\'evy noise, i.e.\ a compensated Poisson random measure of finite intensity, so that the solution evolves deterministically between successive jumps and jumps multiplicatively at the event times. Our main contribution is a stochastic Feynman--Kac representation for the solution, which expresses the random field as the product of the exponential martingale of the jump noise and an expectation over the paths of an independent Brownian motion. The representation converts the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation into an expectation problem, allowing a direct analysis of the front position. Building on this representation, we derive sharp upper and lower bounds for the propagation of the front: for every speed $c>2\sqrt{1+a}$ the solution decays exponentially along the ray $x=ct$, while for every speed $c<2\sqrt{1+a}$ it does not. The two together identify the asymptotic speed in the critical-speed sense: the threshold between exponentially decaying and non-decaying fronts equals $2\sqrt{1+a}$ almost surely, an identity proved without any a priori existence of the limit $R_\delta(t)/t$. The complementary bounds $2\sqrt{\underline{\gamma}}\le c\le2\sqrt{\overline{\gamma}}$ also hold, with $\overline{\gamma},\underline{\gamma}$ explicit in $\epsilon$ and $\mu$. Under the finite-activity assumption, a stopping-time iteration yields pathwise $L^\infty$ bounds and finite-speed propagation of the level sets of the front, which underlie the existence of a travelling wave profile. The framework extends naturally to multi-species cooperative systems, and numerical simulations illustrate the informativeness of the speed bounds.
item.dc:creator: Yuhong Li, Hao Wen, Jianhua Huang
